queue.name: Egypt Israeli Gas Import Pipeline (GASCO / Nitzana Egyptian section)
queue.note: $400M GASCO-built line entirely inside Egypt carrying the expanded NewMed/Leviathan volumes from the Nitzana border into the national grid; roster carries only the Israeli side (P3620 Ramat Hovav, P7864 Nitzana), no Egyptian-side segment. Vetting must decide vs merge into P3620/P7864.

evidence.note: ~$400M pipeline entirely within Egyptian territory, managed by GASCO; construction planned Q4 2025, completion by 2028; to receive additional 130 bcm NewMed/Leviathan volumes through 2040.
Chevron/INGL FID on Israeli Nitzana line (Ramat Hovav to Nitzana, 65 km, ~600 MMcf/d, complete 2028); Egypt separately investing $400M to build the pipeline on its side, GASCO overseeing.
Arabic (attaqa.net): expanded Israel-Egypt deal supports a new pipeline; a local bank and East Mediterranean Gas negotiating a ~$300M loan to finance a new pipeline inside Sinai.

queue.name: Ain Sokhna FSRU Gas Import Pipeline (Sonker berth to national grid)
queue.note: 36-inch, 17-km FSRU-to-grid connector built 2024-2025 at Sonker/Ain Sokhna (GASCO engineering, Petrojet construction); no Sokhna/Sonker/SUMED FSRU connector anywhere in roster. Borderline terminal-connector — vetting to judge pipeline row vs terminal-entry.

evidence.note: 36-inch, 17-km gas import pipeline being installed at Sonker port as conduit for the third FSRU; Petrojet executing with GASCO engineering; two marine and onshore pipelines built at SUMED and Sonker to connect FSRUs to the grid.
Energos Eskimo FSRU nearing grid connection at SUMED berth, Ain Sokhna; new GASCO-built infrastructure injecting regasified LNG into the national grid (may now be operating).

queue.name: Taba–Sharm El-Sheikh Gas Pipeline
queue.note: 220 km, 20-inch South Sinai east-coast transmission trunk (Taba–Nuweiba–Dahab–Sharm El-Sheikh), online early 2007; roster's Sinai lines (P0436 Arish–Taba, P7482 Taba–Aqaba) sit at the Taba node but run the opposite direction, no line south down the coast.

evidence.note: OGJ: GASCO began building the Taba/Sharm El-Sheikh line in 2006; 220 km of 20-inch pipe, up to 6 MMcfd, online early 2007 at ~511M EGP, serving Taba, Nuweiba, Dahab and Sharm El-Sheikh. Single source tracing to Gasco — needs 2nd independent corroboration.

queue.name: Shukeir–Hurghada Gas Pipeline
queue.note: 127 km, 24-inch Red Sea west-coast trunk from Ras Shukeir (Gulf of Suez) to Hurghada, completed 2006; upstream of roster P6034 (Hurghada–Safaga, 24-inch) but a separate physical segment with no roster PID. Vetting to confirm it is not P6034's parent already captured.

evidence.note: OGJ: GASCO completed the Shukeir–Hurghada line in 2006; 127 km of 24-inch pipe, up to 7 MMcfd, ~336M EGP, feeding Red Sea Governorate cities and power stations. Single source tracing to Gasco — needs 2nd independent corroboration.

queue.name: El Sadat–El Fayoum (Dahshour) Gas Pipeline
queue.note: 76 km, 32-inch trunk from El Sadat off-take room south to Dahshour compression station (EGAS Gas Grid Reinforcement); P3928 (Nubaria–Sadat) is upstream and P3930 (New Admin Capital–Dahshur) reaches Dahshour from a different origin — the El Sadat→Dahshour link itself appears uncaptured.

evidence.note: GASCO Environmental Impact Assessment: 76 km, 32-inch, runs south from El Sadat off-take room parallel to SUMED and El Ameriya–Dashour lines through 6th of October City, terminating at Dahshour compression station; to increase gas to Upper Egypt and Cairo.
EIB EGAS Gas Grid Reinforcement project: five large-diameter pipelines ~835 km total; segments include Elnubaria–Elsadat, Elsadat–Elfayoum, and Gerga–Aswan.

queue.name: Libya–Egypt Gas Pipeline
queue.note: Recurring cross-border project family (1997 Altube JV → Nov 2022 NOC Damietta study → Jan 2026 Petrojet–NOC MoU); no Egypt–Libya gas interconnector exists anywhere in GGIT (all Libya rows are domestic or Libya–Italy/Tunisia). Still pre-feasibility/study, no fixed route or capacity — may fall below the add-threshold; vetting to decide.

evidence.note: NOC chairman Bengdara (ADIPEC, Nov 2022): Libya studying two new gas export pipelines — one to Greece, one to Damietta, Egypt — in addition to Greenstream.
Petrojet (Egypt) and NOC (Libya) signed an MoU 25 Jan 2026 at the Libya Energy & Economic Summit; includes studying feasibility of transporting crude oil and natural gas between the two countries.
Project-family history: 1997 Tobruk–Sidi Krir crude plan; 2000 $100m Altube JV to move Libyan crude to Egypt and Egyptian gas to Libya; never built.

queue.name: Gaza Marine–El Arish Offshore Gas Pipeline
queue.note: ~50-60 km subsea export line concept linking Gaza Marine field to the Egyptian grid at El Arish (EGAS 45% operator; MoU 2021, Framework Agreement 2022, Israeli preliminary approval 2023); halted by Gaza war since Oct 2023. Distinct from P5276 (Israel→Gaza supply, opposite direction) and P3657. Development option tied to a stalled field — vetting to weigh vs add-threshold.

evidence.note: Egyptian development option: offshore pipeline linking Gaza Marine to the Egyptian gas network at El Arish, gas swapped in-system for Idku LNG exports; EGAS MoU Feb 2021, Framework Agreement Oct 2022, Israeli preliminary approval June 2023 (Cheiron technical lead); all halted by Gaza war from Oct 2023.
Egypt/PA/Israel talks to revive Gaza Marine with EGAS as 45% operator (PIF 27.5%, CCC 27.5%); gas lines would extend to Al-Arish rather than Israel's Ashdod, Egyptian side processing and marketing.
